newsitem.title: GERMANY: Airtouch gets stake in German telecoms group.
newsitem.headline: Airtouch gets stake in German telecoms group.

text.p: AirTouch Communications, the telecommunications group of the United States, will take a 4.5 percent stake in a Mannesmann-led consortium that holds a minority stake in Arcor Telecommunications, Mannesmann said on Thursday.

AirTouch has the option to raise its stake to nine percent in the year 2000, when Mannesmann's stake in Arcor would rise to 51 percent, replacing the German railway Deutsche Bahn AG as majority shareholder.
Deutsche Bahn AG holds a majority stake of 50.2 percent in Arcor and the Mannesmann-led consortium holds the rest. The consortium includes AT&T Corp and the European Unisource NV group.
The AirTouch stake will come directly from Mannesmann, whose stake in the consortium will be reduced to 55.5 percent.

The consortium has an option to raise its stake in Arcor to 74.9 percent in 1999.

The agreement could make it easier for Mannesmann to ensure that services from its D2 digital cellular phone network are made available for customers of Arcor, which will focus on fixed-wire communications for business customers.
Mannesmann owns 65 percent of Mannesmann Mobilfunk, the D2 operating company, and the rest is owned by AirTouch.

Mannesmann and AirTouch said they expect telecoms services in the future to consist of a comprehensive offering of mobile communications, fixed-wire voice telephony, data services, Internet services and value-added services.

The combination of D2 and Arcor made Mannesmann the only company in Germany able to offer a spectrum of services comparable to those of Deutsche Telekom AG, the recently-listed telecoms group that loses its monopoly in January.
